programs.effectiveChanges: TY2026 (Jan 1, 2026 lien date): basic $180,671, low-income $271,009, income limit $81,131. From the Jan 1, 2027 lien date through lien dates before Jan 1, 2032, SB 296 (signed Sept 28, 2026; adds RTC 205.5.1) suspends most of the 205.5 exemption and substitutes: 50% of the full value of the principal residence up to $1,000,000 (max $500,000 exempt) for a veteran rated 100% (or blind in both eyes / loss of use of two or more limbs / totally disabled from service), and 100% exemption where household income does not exceed $83,474 (indexed). Per the BOE analysis of the July 1, 2026 amendments, the existing 205.5 exemption applies instead where assessed value does not exceed $371,778 and income exceeds the threshold; the August 13 amendment added the $1M cap. Unmarried surviving spouses are covered under conditions. BOE will issue updated BOE-261-G/GNT forms for the 2027 lien date. The 2027 inflation-indexed 205.5 amounts ($185,889 / $278,836 / $83,474) remain relevant for the carve-out and for the sunset after 2031.
programs.note: Dollar modeling for TY2027+: exemptionValue becomes 50% of value capped at $500,000 (fraction 0.5 with a $1M value cap), or 100% for low-income claimants; the current flat $180,671 understates most 2027 claims. SB 296's chapter number could not be read (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returns 403 to automated checks); the Governor's Sept 28, 2026 release and the BOE analysis of the enrolled text are the primary sources used. Row `type: partial` is right through 2026 and for most claimants from 2027; low-income claimants will be 'full' up to $1M of value.
